title: Monitoring Liquidity: TSECF, TSAA and Liquidity Stress Testing

maps.tested: Reported once with an unusual framing.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'liquidity risk trend, seasonal component question', i.e. decomposing a liquidity requirement into trend, seasonal and cyclical components, which sits in the liquidity-planning material. LCR and NSFR mechanics sit in the monitoring reading.

vardeezReading: LTR-7: Moderate. "Maybe one question, maybe none. Do not get hung up on the calculations", though TSEF and TSAA numericals seem important. LTR-9: Moderate. "Know the calculation of contingent liquidity asset buffer", the rest from crash course notes. LTR-10: Important. "Just know the liquidity risk reporting, what are the different reports", basics and interpretation only. LTR-5: Moderate. "L O seventy A and L O seventy B".

los.vardeez: Contingent liquidity via liquid asset buffer: calculation important
Know the different liquidity reports; basics and interpretation only

selectors.name: TSECF and TSAA numerical
selectors.what: Given a purchase, sale or other transaction, say which term structures (TSECF, TSAA, TSLGC) move and by how much: a purchase puts the dirty-price outflow, coupons and redemption in the TSECF and raises the TSAA until expiry.
selectors.theory: What each term structure records: the TSECF the expected positive and negative cash flows by date, the TSECCF their cumulation, the TSAA the quantity of an asset in the bank's possession regardless of ownership; a purchase leaves the TSLGC unaffected.

selectors.name: Trend, seasonal, cyclical liquidity requirement
selectors.what: Forecast deposits and loans as trend + seasonal + cyclical (cyclical = last year's actual - last year's trend-plus-seasonal for that week), then the estimated liquidity deficit (-) or surplus (+) = change in deposits - change in loans.
selectors.theory: Trend is a constant-growth line from at least 10 years of data, seasonal is how the week or month compares with the latest year-end level, cyclical is last year's miss assumed to recur; rising loans and falling deposits drain liquidity, and dropping the cyclical element misstates the requirement.

selectors.name: Repo of an available asset
selectors.what: Cash raised by repoing a bond = N x (Price% + c x tau) x (1 - h), placed in the TSCLGC, with the haircut and the accrued interest since the last coupon; the repayment at maturity = cash x (1 + r_repo x term).
selectors.theory: Repo and sell/buyback cash goes to the TSCLGC, reverse repo and buy/sellback cash to the TSECF; the TSAA falls on a repo, the TSECF is unchanged because coupons stay with the owner bank, and the haircut applies to repo and reverse repo cash only.

selectors.name: TSECCF with initial cash, asset sale
selectors.what: Cumulate the TSECF from Cash(t0) to get the TSECCF, find its most negative point, and size the asset sale that keeps TSLe = TSECCF + TSCLGC non-negative: minimum notional = |most negative TSECCF| / expected price.
selectors.theory: Solvency is read from the cumulated TSECCF starting from initial cash, not from a single period's flow; the sale must cover the most negative point, and the lost coupons and redemption of the sold bond are fed back into the TSECF.

selectors.name: Deterministic versus stochastic cash flows
selectors.what: Classify a cash flow by whether its amount and its time are deterministic or stochastic, with examples such as coupons of risk-free fixed-rate bonds, one-touch option payouts, indexed, credit-related, behavioural and new-business flows.

selectors.name: Liquidity options
selectors.what: Identify liquidity options (committed credit lines, sight and savings deposits, prepayable fixed-rate loans) and their liquidity impact and financial impact on the bank, and which of the two can be hedged.

selectors.name: Contingent liquidity and liquid asset buffer
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'Contingent liquidity via liquid asset buffer: calculation important'
selectors.what: Stressed liquid asset buffer = liquid asset buffer - stressed outflows + stressed inflows, with inflows possibly capped (for example at 75% of outflows under the LCR).
selectors.theory: Contingent liquidity is held as the liquid asset buffer for general obligations under stress; buffer assets need low credit and market risk, easy valuation, an active sizable market and central treasury control.

selectors.name: Types of liquidity risk reports
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'Know the different liquidity reports; basics and interpretation only'
selectors.what: Recognise and interpret the liquidity reports: deposit tracker (loan-to-deposit ratio against a board limit), daily liquidity report, funding maturity gap, funding concentration against a limit, undrawn commitments, and the cash flow survival report.

notSelected: LTR-7 c (liquidity risk definitions, funding cost risk, causes versus sources, cash flow at risk, beyond the TSLe and liquidity generation mechanics used in S3 and S4), LTR-9 a (types of liquidity), LTR-9 c (stress test design, scenarios, governance), LTR-10 a (best practices for reporting) and LTR-10 c (reporting a stress test) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer.
